evidence: The internal premises hold. The whole named spec says deterministic query/request records survive a ledger-only fallback (line 62), requires worker-submitted closure (line 76), restricts every transition citation to the current chunk (line 106), and persists only local deterministic records in a fallback (line 108). Therefore, if chunk B contains the only answer/completion/withdrawal evidence and stores a fallback without its transition, a later disjoint chunk C cannot submit that transition citing B. Searching the entire spec for fallback, retry/resubmit, repair/recovery, reconciliation, replacement, rebuilding and generations finds no same-generation replacement/reprocessing or other closure-recovery contract. Send retries in line 96 concern message identity; generation rebuilding in line 98 does not define recovery of a failed closure and expressly leaves closures generation-local. Line 72 accepts imperfect model recognition, and line 76 accepts semantic uncertainty; neither specifies acceptance of structural loss of an otherwise recognizable closure after fallback. This is significant against the goal of showing unfinished requests and applicable rules (line 5), especially because an explicitly withdrawn rule can remain Active (lines 60, 104). It is Should-fix rather than Blocking: the failure is conditional on fallback, and deterministic source preservation still works.
